answer: To resist Sybil attacks in an AI agent economy, a decentralized social graph acts as a sybil-resistant vine, binding distinct identity nodes together. At dawn, when new agents register, they must demonstrate proof of unique connections to the existing network rather than spawning clones. An attacker faces a massive barrier: forging this deep trust structure requires immense computational timber and real-world credential verification, rendering mass fake-identity creation economically unviable.
